questions.q: Which NCCL collective operation does FSDP use to reconstruct a layer's full parameters from sharded pieces before a forward pass?
options: Broadcast
AllReduce
ReduceScatter
AllGather
questions.explain: AllGather takes a shard on each GPU and produces the full, concatenated result on every GPU — exactly what FSDP needs to reconstruct full parameters before using them in a forward or backward pass.

options: ReduceScatter doesn't perform any reduction at all
AllReduce gives every GPU the full reduced result; ReduceScatter reduces the data but each GPU keeps only its own shard of the result
ReduceScatter only works with Broadcast, not with gradients
AllReduce is slower than ReduceScatter in every case
questions.explain: Both perform a reduction (e.g., sum), but AllReduce distributes the full reduced result to every GPU, while ReduceScatter gives each GPU only its own shard — which is what FSDP uses for sharded gradients.

questions.q: What does setting NCCL_DEBUG=INFO let you observe?
options: The model's current loss value
Which network path and algorithm NCCL selected, visible in its startup log output
The number of training tokens processed so far
The GPU temperature
questions.explain: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO turns on verbose logging that shows topology discovery and the ring/tree communication pattern NCCL built, including which network path (e.g., InfiniBand vs. sockets) it chose.

questions.q: In NCCL_DEBUG=INFO output, what would it mean if the log showed 'NET/Socket' being used instead of 'NET/IB' on solara-train?
options: This is the expected, fastest configuration
It indicates NCCL fell back to a slower network path instead of using InfiniBand, signaling a possible misconfiguration
It means the job completed successfully
It means FSDP is disabled
questions.explain: solara-train's fast inter-node path is InfiniBand. Seeing NET/Socket instead of NET/IB in the debug log suggests NCCL fell back to a much slower path, which usually points to an InfiniBand configuration problem worth investigating.

questions.q: How does NCCL decide whether to route communication over NVLink or InfiniBand for a given pair of GPUs?
options: The training script must explicitly specify the physical path for every operation
NCCL inspects the hardware topology at startup and automatically builds its communication pattern around the fastest available path
It always uses InfiniBand, even for GPUs on the same node
It picks randomly between available paths
questions.explain: NCCL automatically discovers the hardware topology (which GPUs share NVLink vs. which only reach each other over InfiniBand) at startup and builds its ring/tree pattern to prefer the fastest links, without requiring the training code to know the physical layout.
